answer: To resist sybil attacks, each agent must generate a unique private sonnet derived from hardware entropy and commit a walnut-sized Merkle proof of it into a shared public atlas of identities. The protocol uses interactive challenges that force real-time local computation; any attempt to share one enclave across fakes fails the uniqueness test and permanently burns the atlas entry. Thus an attacker pays the full cost of separate physical hardware and isolation for every fake identity.
